title: Work IQ: retrieve tool gives agents Microsoft 365 grounding content
summary: The roadmap details, retrieval behaviour, billing prerequisites and documented controls are supported. Minor corrections should simplify the Graph call, acknowledge the documented workIQ service category and remove a consent-governance checklist step that has no controls-table row.

claims.claim: Roadmap item Work IQ: Retrieve plans to enable agents to retrieve relevant Microsoft 365 content and context through Work IQ.
claims.quote: Enable agents to retrieve relevant Microsoft 365 content and context through Work IQ.

claims.claim: The roadmap record has no more-info link identifying the MCP retrieve tool.
claims.quote: "moreInfoLink": null

claims.quote: "previewDate": "October CY2026"

claims.claim: Retrieval uses the signed-in user's access and does not grant access to otherwise inaccessible content.
claims.quote: Retrieval runs in the context of the signed-in user and doesn't grant access to content that the user can't otherwise access.

claims.quote: Model-friendly Markdown with inline citations.

claims.claim: The separate ask tool returns a Copilot or agent answer.

claims.claim: Calling users must be assigned to a spending policy that includes Work IQ API.
claims.quote: Set up usage-based billing for Copilot Credits and assign the calling users to a spending policy that includes Work IQ API.

claims.claim: Where the organization uses Work IQ MCP policy, Work IQ MCP must be enabled.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: Admin-opt-in describes the required billing, spending-policy and consent setup rather than an asserted default for the MCP policy toggle.
claims.quote: Set up usage-based billing for Copilot Credits and assign the calling users to a spending policy that includes Work IQ API. ... Register a client application and grant the delegated `WorkIQAgent.Ask` permission.

claims.where: Why it matters; Open questions: MCP policy default
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether the tenant Work IQ MCP policy toggle is on or off by default.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ MCP" policy "default" enabled. Read policy-governance-mcp, retrieve and MCP overview; results state default mutation restrictions but not the initial on/off state of the tenant policy toggle.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Policy reaches the tenant policy surface.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Agents > Tools. ... In the tools registry, select Work IQ MCP. ... On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the Policy tab when it's available.

claims.claim: The initial Work IQ MCP policy control is tenant-level.
claims.quote: In the initial release, Work IQ MCP provides tenant-level policy control.

claims.claim: Per-user, per-app, per-agent and scenario-specific policy templates are not part of the initial policy surface.
claims.quote: Per-user, per-app, per-agent, or scenario-specific policy templates aren't part of the initial policy control surface.

claims.claim: The instructions qualify the Policy tab with 'when it's available'.
claims.quote: On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the Policy tab when it's available.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: A saved Work IQ MCP policy change can take up to 24 hours to apply across the tenant.
claims.quote: After you save the setting, it can take up to 24 hours for the policy change to apply across your tenant.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: UI-only qualification; Open questions
claims.claim: No API for reading or changing the Work IQ MCP tenant policy was found in Microsoft's documentation.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ MCP" policy API Graph update Allowed Disallowed; site:learn.microsoft.com/graph "Work IQ" "policy"; "Work IQ MCP" "policy" "API" "PATCH". Read policy-governance-mcp and MCP overview; no policy API operation was returned.

claims.claim: The policy page says mutation operations including create, update, delete and action requests are blocked by default.
claims.quote: By default, mutation operations aren't allowed for safety. This restriction includes create, update, delete, and action requests that modify data, such as sending email.

claims.claim: Administrators can enable supported mutation scenarios through tenant policy.
claims.quote: Administrators can enable supported mutation scenarios through tenant policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center when those capabilities are needed.

claims.claim: Result source metadata can include sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: `sensitivityLabel` | object | Sensitivity-label metadata for the source, when available.

claims.claim: Result source metadata can include a contentProtection evaluation value.
claims.quote: `contentProtection` | string | The content-protection evaluation result, when available.

claims.claim: Learn tells developers not to treat missing, failed, blocked or unrecognized contentProtection values as an allow decision.
claims.quote: Don't treat a missing, failed, blocked, or unrecognized value as an allow decision.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; summary; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Work IQ API uses consumption-based billing measured in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: You pay for use of the Work IQ API through a usage-based model that uses Copilot Credits.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Work IQ API access is independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing.
claims.quote: Work IQ API access is independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing and available through usage-based billing.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Work IQ API consumes Copilot Credits shared with other eligible services.
claims.quote: Work IQ API usage consumes Copilot Credits shared with other eligible services.

claims.claim: Supported usage-based services such as Cowork and Work IQ API can use prepaid credits or pay-as-you-go funding managed in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Depending on the service, organizations can use fixed licensing, the Copilot Credit Pre-purchase Plan (P3), pay-as-you-go billing, prepaid capacity packs, or supported combinations of these billing methods.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A credit rate specific to retrieve, including a strategy-specific rate, was not found as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "retrieve" "credits" rate pricing; "retrieve" "Work IQ" "rate" "Copilot Credits". Read retrieve, Work IQ access/pricing, API overview and billing overview; no retrieve-specific rate found. The licensing short-link fetch was denied.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > + Add spending policy opens spending-policy creation.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Cost Management. ... Select the Configuration tab and then select + Add spending policy.

claims.claim: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} updates periodLimit, perUserLimit or billingMethods using an If-Match ETag.
claims.quote: PATCH /copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} ... If-Match | The ETag of the spending policy. Required. ... The following properties can be updated: displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and billingMethods.
claims.fix: Set controls[1].api.call and the rendered call to 'PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id}'. Add to its note: 'The request body sets periodLimit or perUserLimit to change spending limits; If-Match supplies the policy ETag.' Leave complete funding-change requirements to the linked reference.

claims.claim: The Copilot Cost Management API used in the row is beta.
claims.quote: APIs under the `/beta` version are subject to change.

claims.claim: The update operation requires CopilotCostManagement-Policy.ReadWrite.All.
claims.quote: Delegated (work or school account) | CopilotCostManagement-Policy.ReadWrite.All

claims.claim: Microsoft says using this beta API in production applications is not supported.
claims.quote: Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Spending policies control eligible users and services and provide policy-level and optional per-user monthly limits.
claims.quote: Select the agents and services that users and groups in this policy can access. ... Select the monthly spending limit for this policy. ... Select monthly budget limits for users (optional).

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Auto-apply new services is selected by default and automatically adds newly supported services to spending policies.
claims.quote: By default, the Auto-apply new services toggle is selected for spending policies. ... When the setting is on, newly supported Microsoft Copilot services and agents are automatically added to the policy.

claims.claim: Spending policies are limit-based controls and do not reserve or allocate Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Spending policies are limit-based controls and don't reserve or allocate Copilot Credits to users or groups.

claims.claim: Consumption through custom integrations that call Work IQ directly appears under Work IQ API.
claims.quote: Coding agents or custom integrations that call Work IQ directly: Consumption through that connection appears under Work IQ API.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: variable task costs
claims.claim: One request can involve multiple tool calls and reasoning steps, so cost per task varies.
claims.quote: One user request can involve multiple tool calls and reasoning steps. Work IQ includes deterministic operations and variable-cost contextual reasoning, so a prompt isn't necessarily a single fixed-price operation.

claims.claim: Application-only authentication is not supported for the Work IQ API.
claims.quote: Application-only authentication isn't supported.

claims.claim: No page found maps the API's service settings specifically to Work IQ API as an individual billable service.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "serviceSettings" "workIQ". Read spendingpolicyservicesetting: serviceId identifies a category such as workIQ, and multiple billable services can share a category; it does not identify Work IQ API individually.
claims.fix: Replace 'This briefing found no page saying that API's service settings expose Work IQ API specifically.' with 'The API documents a governed-service category named workIQ; multiple billable services can share a category.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/cost-management/resources/spendingpolicyservicesetting. Do not equate the category with an individual billable service.

claims.claim: Capabilities and strategy are chosen in individual application requests, not tenant admin settings.
claims.quote: The strategy parameter controls where Work IQ searches. ... Use capabilities to provide a source allow list for one retrieval request.

claims.claim: The roadmap lists no US Government cloud, without asserting exclusion from those clouds.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.claim: The variable cost rating corresponds to metered Copilot Credit consumption.
claims.quote: Work IQ cost is variable based on usage ... Work IQ API usage consumes Copilot Credits shared with other eligible services.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, delegated consent bullet
claims.claim: The consent-governance decision in the checklist is represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Decide who may grant the delegated `WorkIQAgent.Ask` permission for client apps. ... Controls table: Whether Work IQ MCP tools ... are allowed in the tenant; Who can consume Copilot Credits ... and the monthly limits.
claims.fix: Remove the Before rollout bullet 'Decide who may grant the delegated `WorkIQAgent.Ask` permission for client apps.' Keep the permission prerequisite and security discussion unchanged; the consent-governance decision has no corresponding control row.

claims.where: summary; controls[0].governs; Open questions: policy and retrieve

claims.quote: `retrieve` isn't returned by `tools/list` | Verify tenant availability and that Work IQ MCP isn't blocked

claims.claim: Learn recommends surfacing policy-denied responses instead of automatically retrying them.
claims.quote: Surface policy denials and authentication failures instead of retrying them as transient errors.

claims.claim: Developers should call tools/list and confirm retrieve is available.
claims.quote: Call `tools/list` after connecting and confirm that `retrieve` is available.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, monthly limits
claims.claim: Users reaching the spending limit lose access to agents and services for the rest of the month until credits reset.
claims.quote: When users hit the limit, they lose access to agents and services for the rest of the month until credits reset on the first of the month.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout, consumption monitoring
claims.claim: The Cost management dashboard in the Microsoft 365 admin center supports monitoring Work IQ API usage.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft admin center, Copilot > Cost management, admins can monitor Copilot Credit consumption and manage spending associated with the supported services such as Cowork, running apps hosted on the Copilot Managed Runtime, and Work IQ API.

claims.claim: Retrieve is a read-style tool returning grounding content rather than modifying data.
claims.quote: The Work IQ MCP `retrieve` tool searches data that the signed-in user can access and returns grounding content for an AI agent.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions, mutation qualification
claims.claim: The policy page's mutation-default discussion does not specifically identify retrieve.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ MCP" policy "default" enabled; "Work IQ MCP" policy API Graph update Allowed Disallowed. Read the full policy-governance-mcp page: its mutation discussion identifies create, update, delete and action requests, not retrieve.
